+"""Dataset preparation and strict, evidence-grounded validation."""
+import json
+import math
+import re
+from pathlib import Path
+
+from backend.services.git_evidence import git, resolve
+from backend.services.repository_analyzer import analyze_repository_data
+
+TASKS = ("intent", "scope", "recovery")
+TARGETS = {"repositories": 25, "intent": 40, "scope": 30, "recovery": 20, "commits_approximate": 1800}
+
+
+def write_json(path, value):
+    path = Path(path)
+    path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
+    path.write_text(json.dumps(value, indent=2, ensure_ascii=False, allow_nan=False) + "\n", encoding="utf-8")
+
+
+def read_json(path):
+    return json.loads(Path(path).read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
+
+
+def require(condition, message):
+    if not condition:
+        raise ValueError(message)
+
+
+def nonempty(value):
+    return isinstance(value, str) and bool(value.strip())
+
+
+def load_dataset(directory, allow_unlabelled=False, tasks=TASKS):
+    directory = Path(directory).resolve()
+    manifest = read_json(directory / "repositories.json")
+    require(isinstance(manifest, dict) and manifest.get("schema_version") == 1, "Unsupported dataset schema")
+    repos = manifest["repositories"]
+    require(isinstance(repos, list) and bool(repos), "No source repositories registered")
+    repo_map = {}
+    unique_sources = set()
+    origins = set()
+    for repo in repos:
+        require(nonempty(repo.get("id")) and repo["id"] not in repo_map, "Duplicate/missing repository ID")
+        path = (directory / repo["path"]).resolve()
+        require(path not in unique_sources, "Duplicate source repository path")
+        unique_sources.add(path)
+        resolve(path, repo["revision"])
+        require(nonempty(repo.get("source")), "Repository source/provenance required")
+        origin = repo["source"].rstrip("/").removesuffix(".git")
+        require(origin not in origins, "Duplicate repository source/origin")
+        origins.add(origin)
+        repo_map[repo["id"]] = {**repo, "resolved_path": str(path)}
+    cases = {task: read_json(directory / f"{task}_cases.json") for task in TASKS}
+    packs, ids, cache = {}, set(), {}
+    pending = []
+    for task in TASKS:
+        require(isinstance(cases[task], list), f"{task}: cases must be a JSON list")
+        for case in cases[task]:
+            cid = case.get("case_id")
+            require(isinstance(cid, str) and re.fullmatch(r"[A-Za-z0-9_-]+", cid) and cid not in ids, "Invalid/duplicate case ID")
+            ids.add(cid)
+            require(case.get("repository") in repo_map, f"{cid}: unknown repository")
+            repo = repo_map[case["repository"]]
+            rev = resolve(repo["resolved_path"], case.get("revision"))
+            reachable = git(repo["resolved_path"], "rev-list", repo["revision"]).splitlines()
+            require(rev in reachable, f"{cid}: revision outside pinned repository history")
+            if task == "intent":
+                require(nonempty(case.get("file")) and isinstance(case.get("region"), list) and len(case["region"]) == 2,
+                        f"{cid}: file and [start,end] region required")
+            key = (repo["id"], rev, case.get("file") if task == "intent" else None, tuple(case.get("region", [])) if task == "intent" else ())
+            if key not in cache:
+                cache[key] = analyze_repository_data(repo["resolved_path"], revision=rev,
+                    file=case.get("file") if task == "intent" else None,
+                    region=case.get("region") if task == "intent" else None, as_of=manifest["as_of"])
+            pack = {**cache[key], "repository": repo["id"], "source_repository": repo["source"]}
+            if task == "scope":
+                require(case.get("diff") == pack["diff"], f"{cid}: diff must exactly match pinned commit")
+                require(set(case.get("gold_hunks", {})) == {h["id"] for h in pack["hunks"]}, f"{cid}: gold hunk IDs differ from Git")
+                require(bool(pack["hunks"]), f"{cid}: no text hunks to classify")
+                pack["task"] = case.get("task")
+            packs[cid] = pack
+            annotation = case.get("annotation", {})
+            require(annotation.get("status") in {"pending", "labelled"}, f"{cid}: annotation status must be pending or labelled")
+            if annotation["status"] != "labelled":
+                pending.append(cid)
+                continue
+            require(nonempty(annotation.get("annotator")) and nonempty(annotation.get("rationale")), f"{cid}: human annotator and evidence rationale required")
+            if task == "intent":
+                require(nonempty(case.get("gold_intent")), f"{cid}: gold_intent required")
+                require(isinstance(case.get("accepted_intents"), list) and bool(case["accepted_intents"]) and all(nonempty(x) for x in case["accepted_intents"]), f"{cid}: accepted_intents required")
+                require(case["gold_intent"] in case["accepted_intents"], f"{cid}: gold_intent must be accepted")
+                supporting = case.get("supporting_commits")
+                require(isinstance(supporting, list) and bool(supporting), f"{cid}: supporting commits required")
+                for sha in [case.get("introducing_commit"), *supporting]:

software projects.\n+\n+Built with **LangGraph, FastAPI, and React**, this project moves beyond traditional Git tools by synthesizing commit history, structural code patches, and file dependency graphs to explain *why* code exists, not just *what* changed.\n+\n+---\n+\n+## 🌟 Key Features\n+\n+1. **🧠 Intent Reconstruction (Intent Agent)**\n+   * Deduces the developer's original intent behind code changes using an Intent-Oriented Chain-of-Thought strategy.\n+   * Provides explicit evidence citations (referencing exact lines of code and commit SHAs) to prove its conclusions.\n+\n+2. **⚠️ tools by synthesizing commit history, structural code patches, and file dependency graphs to explain *why* code exists, not just *what* changed.\n+\n+---\n+\n+## 🌟 Key Features\n+\n+1. **🧠 Intent Reconstruction (Intent Agent)**\n+   * Deduces the developer's original intent behind code changes using an Intent-Oriented Chain-of-Thought strategy.\n+   * Provides explicit evidence citations (referencing exact lines of code and commit SHAs) to prove its conclusions.\n+\n+2. **⚠️ Scope Creep Detection (Scope Agent)**\n+   * Compares the stated goal of a commit against the actual structural code changes.\n+   * Flags unrelated file modifications and architectural deviations that fall outside the bounds of the original task.\n+\n+3. **♻️ Abandoned Project Recovery (Recovery Agent)**\n+   * Analyzes incomplete or abandoned repositories to calculate a heuristic **Health Score**.\n+   * Replaces naive inactivity metrics (like commit frequency or stars) with deep structural indicators like code completeness, unresolved TODOs, and architectural continuity.\n+   * **Multi-Project Comparison:** Ranks multiple repositories to recommend which project holds the highest technical viability for completion.\n+\n+4. **🕸️ Visual Relationship Graph**\n+   * Renders a physics-based, 2D force-directed graph connecting commits to their modified files, allowing developers to visually spot high-risk architectural bottlenecks.\n+\n+5. **📊 Empirical Evaluation Suite (Research Ready)**\n+   * Includes a built-in evaluation framework for academic research.\n+   * Compares the Agentic System's accuracy against standard Git Baselines and zero-shot LLM Baselines.\n+\n+---\n+\n+## 🏗️ System Architecture\n+\n+* **Backend:** FastAPI, Python, SQLite\n+* **AI Orchestration:** LangGraph An Agentic AI Framework for Code Intent Analysis, Scope Creep Detection, and Software Project Recovery\n+\n+## 1. Abstract\n+Understanding the historical intent behind software code is challenging because conventional version-control tools primarily describe what changed rather than why a change was introduced. Developers may also struggle to identify changes that exceed the original task scope and to assess whether abandoned software projects are worth recovering. This work proposes an agentic AI framework that analyzes Git repository history, code diffs, file evolution, and repository metadata to reconstruct code intent, detect potential scope creep, and assess project recovery potential. The framework uses specialized AI agents coordinated through a LangGraph workflow-based architecture and produces evidence-linked conclusions. The system is evaluated against Git-based and single-prompt LLM baselines using intent reconstruction, scope detection, and evidence-support metrics. The experimental results demonstrate the effectiveness of combining multiple repository evidence sources with agentic reasoning.\n+\n+## 2. Problem Statement\n+Developers often struggle to understand why old code was written, identify changes that go beyond the original task, and decide which abandoned software project is worth completing. Existing Git tools mainly show what changed, but not the complete context and reasoning behind the code.\n+\n+## 4. Related Work\n+**1. Intent Reconstruction & Commit Untangling**\n+The challenge of deducing developer intent and untangling composite commits has an established lineage in software engineering literature. Early structural and graph-based approaches laid the foundation for rationale-mining from version control histories (Barnett et al., 2015; Dias et al., 2015). More recently, research has shifted toward semantic intent extraction. For instance, Dhaouadi et al. (2023) explored rationale-mining from commit messages via knowledge graphs, while Fan et al. (2024) focused on detecting hidden dependencies. Most relevant to our work is *Atomizer* (Zhu et al., 2026), an LLM-based collaborative multi-agent framework that uses an Intent-Oriented Chain-of-Thought (IO-CoT) strategy to iteratively untangle composite commits. Similarly, *ColaUntangle* (Hou et al., 2024) employs explicit and implicit dependency agents, alongside a reviewer agent, to synthesize commit semantics through iterative consultation.\n+\n+**2. Multi-Stage Reasoning with LLM Agents**\n+The use of specialized LLM agents for interpreting repository semantics has recently gained traction. *VIC-RAGENT* (Chen et al., 2026) proposes a multi-stage reasoning pipeline utilizing specialized \"Code Analyst\" and \"Target Analyst\" agents to detect Vulnerability-Inducing Commits (VICs). \n+\n+**3. Software Project Abandonment & Viability**\n+Prior research heavily relies on fixed inactivity thresholds to classify project abandonment. However, empirical investigations challenge this naive assumption. Avelino et al. (2019) analyzed 1,932 popular GitHub projects, finding that 16% were abandoned by their original core developers, yet 41% of those successfully survived due to community intervention. This indicates that inactivity alone is a volatile signal.\n+\n+## 5. Research Gap\n+Existing approaches generally fall into these categories:\n+- Git tools → show history and structural changes\n+- Code summarization → explains what the code does\n+- LLM QA tools → answer ad-hoc questions about repositories\n+\n+**Gap:** They do not provide one cohesive, evidence-based workflow that combines Code Intent Reconstruction + Scope Creep Detection + Abandoned Project Recovery utilizing multi-agent AI reasoning.\n+\n+## 6. An Agentic AI Framework for Code Intent Analysis, Scope Creep Detection, and Software Project Recovery\n+\n+## 1. Abstract\n+Understanding the historical intent behind software code is challenging because conventional version-control tools primarily describe what changed rather than why a change was introduced. Developers may also struggle to identify changes that exceed the original task scope and to assess whether abandoned software projects are worth recovering. This work proposes an agentic AI framework that analyzes Git repository history, code diffs, file evolution, and repository metadata to reconstruct code intent, detect potential scope creep, and assess project recovery potential. The framework uses specialized AI agents coordinated through a LangGraph workflow-based architecture and produces evidence-linked conclusions. The system is evaluated against Git-based and single-prompt LLM baselines using intent reconstruction, scope detection, and evidence-support metrics. The experimental results demonstrate the effectiveness of combining multiple repository evidence sources with agentic reasoning.\n+\n+## 2. Introduction\n+[To be expanded based on problem statement...]\n+\n+## 3. Problem Statement\n+Developers often struggle to understand why old code was written, identify changes that go beyond the original task, and decide which abandoned software project is worth completing. Existing Git tools mainly show what changed, but not the complete context and reasoning behind the code.\n+\n+## 4. Related Work\n+**1. Intent Reconstruction & Commit Untangling**\n+The challenge of deducing developer intent and untangling composite commits has an established lineage in software engineering literature. Early structural and graph-based approaches laid the foundation for rationale-mining from version control histories (Barnett et al., 2015; Dias et al., 2015). More recently, research has shifted toward semantic intent extraction. For instance, Dhaouadi et al. (2023) explored rationale-mining from commit messages via knowledge graphs, while Fan et al. (2024) focused on detecting hidden dependencies. Most relevant to our work is *Atomizer* (Zhu et al., 2026), an LLM-based collaborative multi-agent framework that uses an Intent-Oriented Chain-of-Thought (IO-CoT) strategy to iteratively untangle composite commits. Similarly, *ColaUntangle* (Hou et al., 2024) employs explicit and implicit dependency agents, alongside a reviewer agent, to synthesize commit semantics through iterative consultation.\n+\n+**2. Multi-Stage Reasoning with LLM Agents**\n+The use of specialized LLM agents for interpreting repository semantics has recently gained traction. *VIC-RAGENT* (Chen et al., 2026) proposes a multi-stage reasoning pipeline utilizing specialized \"Code Analyst\" and \"Target Analyst\" agents to detect Vulnerability-Inducing Commits (VICs). \n+\n+**3. Software Project Abandonment & Viability**\n+Prior research heavily relies on fixed inactivity thresholds to classify project abandonment. However, empirical investigations challenge this naive assumption. Avelino et al. (2019) analyzed 1,932 popular GitHub projects, finding that 16% were abandoned by their original core developers, yet 41% of those successfully survived due to community intervention. This indicates that inactivity alone is a volatile signal.\n+\n+## 5. Research Gap\n+Existing approaches generally fall into these categories:\n+- Git tools → show history and structural changes\n+- Code summarization → explains what the code does\n+- LLM QA tools → answer ad-hoc questions about repositories\n+\n+**Gap:** They do not provide one cohesive, evidence-based workflow that combines Code Intent Reconstruction + Scope Creep Detection + Abandoned Project Recovery utilizing multi-agent AI reasoning.\n+\n+## 6. Proposed Methodology & System Architecture\n+\n+```text\n+                 Git Repository\n+                       │\n+                       ▼\n+              Repository Analyzer\n+                       │\n+        ┌──────────────┼──────────────┐\n+        ▼              ▼              ▼\n+   Commit History   Code Diffs    File History\n+        │              │              │\n+        └──────────────┼──────────────┘\n+                       ▼\n+                Agent Workflow (LangGraph)\n+                       │\n+        ┌──────────────┼──────────────┐\n+        ▼              ▼              ▼\n+   Intent Agent    Scope Agent   Recovery Agent\n+        │              │              │\n+        └──────────────┼──────────────┘\n+                       ▼\n+             Evidence-Based Results\n+                       │\n+                       ▼\n+          Dashboard + Recommendations\n+```\n+\n+## 7. graphs to explain *why* code exists, not just *what* changed.\n+\n+---\n+\n+## 🌟 Key Features\n+\n+1. **🧠 Intent Reconstruction (Intent Agent)**\n+   * Deduces the developer's original intent behind code changes using an Intent-Oriented Chain-of-Thought strategy.\n+   * Provides explicit evidence citations (referencing exact lines of code and commit SHAs) to prove its conclusions.\n+\n+2. **⚠️ +      "text": "@@ -0,0 +1,100 @@\n+# 🏺 Agentic Code Archaeology\n+\n+**Agentic Code Archaeology** is an AI-powered, multi-agent system designed to reconstruct the intent behind legacy code, detect scope creep in commits, and evaluate the technical viability of recovering abandoned software projects.\n+\n+Built with **LangGraph, FastAPI, and React**, this project moves beyond traditional Git tools by synthesizing commit history, structural code patches, and file dependency graphs to explain *why* code exists, not just *what* changed.\n+\n+---\n+\n+## 🌟 Key Features\n+\n+1. **🧠 Intent Reconstruction (Intent Agent)**\n+   * Deduces the developer's original intent behind code changes using an Intent-Oriented Chain-of-Thought strategy.\n+   * Provides explicit evidence citations (referencing exact lines of code and commit SHAs) to prove its conclusions.\n+\n+2. **⚠️ Scope Creep Detection (Scope Agent)**\n+   * Compares the stated goal of a commit against the actual structural code changes.\n+   * Flags unrelated file modifications and architectural deviations that fall outside the bounds of the original task.\n+\n+3. **♻️ Abandoned Project Recovery (Recovery Agent)**\n+   * Analyzes incomplete or abandoned repositories to calculate a heuristic **Health Score**.\n+   * Replaces naive inactivity metrics (like commit frequency or stars) with deep structural indicators like code completeness, unresolved TODOs, and architectural continuity.\n+   * **Multi-Project Comparison:** Ranks multiple repositories to recommend which project holds the highest technical viability for completion.\n+\n+4. **🕸️ Visual Relationship Graph**\n+   * Renders a physics-based, 2D force-directed graph connecting commits to their modified files, allowing developers to visually spot high-risk architectural bottlenecks.\n+\n+5. **📊 Empirical Evaluation Suite (Research Ready)**\n+   * Includes a built-in evaluation framework for academic research.\n+   * Compares the Agentic System's accuracy against standard Git Baselines and zero-shot LLM Baselines.\n+\n+---\n+\n+## 🏗️ System Architecture\n+\n+* **Backend:** FastAPI, Python, SQLite\n+* **AI Orchestration:** LangGraph An Agentic AI Framework for Code Intent Analysis, Scope Creep Detection, and Software Project Recovery\n+\n+## 1. Abstract\n+Understanding the historical intent behind software code is challenging because conventional version-control tools primarily describe what changed rather than why a change was introduced. Developers may also struggle to identify changes that exceed the original task scope and to assess whether abandoned software projects are worth recovering. This work proposes an agentic AI framework that analyzes Git repository history, code diffs, file evolution, and repository metadata to reconstruct code intent, detect potential scope creep, and assess project recovery potential. The framework uses specialized AI agents coordinated through a LangGraph workflow-based architecture and produces evidence-linked conclusions. The system is evaluated against Git-based and single-prompt LLM baselines using intent reconstruction, scope detection, and evidence-support metrics. The experimental results demonstrate the effectiveness of combining multiple repository evidence sources with agentic reasoning.\n+\n+## 2. Problem Statement\n+Developers often struggle to understand why old code was written, identify changes that go beyond the original task, and decide which abandoned software project is worth completing. Existing Git tools mainly show what changed, but not the complete context and reasoning behind the code.\n+\n+## 4. Related Work\n+**1. Intent Reconstruction & Commit Untangling**\n+The challenge of deducing developer intent and untangling composite commits has an established lineage in software engineering literature. Early structural and graph-based approaches laid the foundation for rationale-mining from version control histories (Barnett et al., 2015; Dias et al., 2015). More recently, research has shifted toward semantic intent extraction. For instance, Dhaouadi et al. (2023) explored rationale-mining from commit messages via knowledge graphs, while Fan et al. (2024) focused on detecting hidden dependencies. Most relevant to our work is *Atomizer* (Zhu et al., 2026), an LLM-based collaborative multi-agent framework that uses an Intent-Oriented Chain-of-Thought (IO-CoT) strategy to iteratively untangle composite commits. Similarly, *ColaUntangle* (Hou et al., 2024) employs explicit and implicit dependency agents, alongside a reviewer agent, to synthesize commit semantics through iterative consultation.\n+\n+**2. Multi-Stage Reasoning with LLM Agents**\n+The use of specialized LLM agents for interpreting repository semantics has recently gained traction. *VIC-RAGENT* (Chen et al., 2026) proposes a multi-stage reasoning pipeline utilizing specialized \"Code Analyst\" and \"Target Analyst\" agents to detect Vulnerability-Inducing Commits (VICs). \n+\n+**3. Software Project Abandonment & Viability**\n+Prior research heavily relies on fixed inactivity thresholds to classify project abandonment. However, empirical investigations challenge this naive assumption. Avelino et al. (2019) analyzed 1,932 popular GitHub projects, finding that 16% were abandoned by their original core developers, yet 41% of those successfully survived due to community intervention. This indicates that inactivity alone is a volatile signal.\n+\n+## 5. Research Gap\n+Existing approaches generally fall into these categories:\n+- Git tools → show history and structural changes\n+- Code summarization → explains what the code does\n+- LLM QA tools → answer ad-hoc questions about repositories\n+\n+**Gap:** They do not provide one cohesive, evidence-based workflow that combines Code Intent Reconstruction + Scope Creep Detection + Abandoned Project Recovery utilizing multi-agent AI reasoning.\n+\n+## 6. An Agentic AI Framework for Code Intent Analysis, Scope Creep Detection, and Software Project Recovery\n+\n+## 1. Abstract\n+Understanding the historical intent behind software code is challenging because conventional version-control tools primarily describe what changed rather than why a change was introduced. Developers may also struggle to identify changes that exceed the original task scope and to assess whether abandoned software projects are worth recovering. This work proposes an agentic AI framework that analyzes Git repository history, code diffs, file evolution, and repository metadata to reconstruct code intent, detect potential scope creep, and assess project recovery potential. The framework uses specialized AI agents coordinated through a LangGraph workflow-based architecture and produces evidence-linked conclusions. The system is evaluated against Git-based and single-prompt LLM baselines using intent reconstruction, scope detection, and evidence-support metrics. The experimental results demonstrate the effectiveness of combining multiple repository evidence sources with agentic reasoning.\n+\n+## 2. Introduction\n+[To be expanded based on problem statement...]\n+\n+## 3. Problem Statement\n+Developers often struggle to understand why old code was written, identify changes that go beyond the original task, and decide which abandoned software project is worth completing. Existing Git tools mainly show what changed, but not the complete context and reasoning behind the code.\n+\n+## 4. Related Work\n+**1. Intent Reconstruction & Commit Untangling**\n+The challenge of deducing developer intent and untangling composite commits has an established lineage in software engineering literature. Early structural and graph-based approaches laid the foundation for rationale-mining from version control histories (Barnett et al., 2015; Dias et al., 2015). More recently, research has shifted toward semantic intent extraction. For instance, Dhaouadi et al. (2023) explored rationale-mining from commit messages via knowledge graphs, while Fan et al. (2024) focused on detecting hidden dependencies. Most relevant to our work is *Atomizer* (Zhu et al., 2026), an LLM-based collaborative multi-agent framework that uses an Intent-Oriented Chain-of-Thought (IO-CoT) strategy to iteratively untangle composite commits. Similarly, *ColaUntangle* (Hou et al., 2024) employs explicit and implicit dependency agents, alongside a reviewer agent, to synthesize commit semantics through iterative consultation.\n+\n+**2. Multi-Stage Reasoning with LLM Agents**\n+The use of specialized LLM agents for interpreting repository semantics has recently gained traction. *VIC-RAGENT* (Chen et al., 2026) proposes a multi-stage reasoning pipeline utilizing specialized \"Code Analyst\" and \"Target Analyst\" agents to detect Vulnerability-Inducing Commits (VICs). \n+\n+**3. Software Project Abandonment & Viability**\n+Prior research heavily relies on fixed inactivity thresholds to classify project abandonment. However, empirical investigations challenge this naive assumption. Avelino et al. (2019) analyzed 1,932 popular GitHub projects, finding that 16% were abandoned by their original core developers, yet 41% of those successfully survived due to community intervention. This indicates that inactivity alone is a volatile signal.\n+\n+## 5. Research Gap\n+Existing approaches generally fall into these categories:\n+- Git tools → show history and structural changes\n+- Code summarization → explains what the code does\n+- LLM QA tools → answer ad-hoc questions about repositories\n+\n+**Gap:** They do not provide one cohesive, evidence-based workflow that combines Code Intent Reconstruction + Scope Creep Detection + Abandoned Project Recovery utilizing multi-agent AI reasoning.\n+\n+## 6. Proposed Methodology & System Architecture\n+\n+```text\n+                 Git Repository\n+                       │\n+                       ▼\n+              Repository Analyzer\n+                       │\n+        ┌──────────────┼──────────────┐\n+        ▼              ▼              ▼\n+   Commit History   Code Diffs    File History\n+        │              │              │\n+        └──────────────┼──────────────┘\n+                       ▼\n+                Agent Workflow (LangGraph)\n+                       │\n+        ┌──────────────┼──────────────┐\n+        ▼              ▼              ▼\n+   Intent Agent    Scope Agent   Recovery Agent\n+        │              │              │\n+        └──────────────┼──────────────┘\n+                       ▼\n+             Evidence-Based Results\n+                       │\n+                       ▼\n+          Dashboard + Recommendations\n+```\n+\n+## 7. An Agentic AI Framework for Code Intent Analysis, Scope Creep Detection, and Software Project Recovery\n+\n+## 1. Abstract\n+Understanding the historical intent behind software code is challenging because conventional version-control tools primarily describe what changed rather than why a change was introduced. Developers may also struggle to identify changes that exceed the original task scope and to assess whether abandoned software projects are worth recovering. This work proposes an agentic AI framework that analyzes Git repository history, code diffs, file evolution, and repository metadata to reconstruct code intent, detect potential scope creep, and assess project recovery potential. The framework uses specialized AI agents coordinated through a LangGraph workflow-based architecture and produces evidence-linked conclusions. The system is evaluated against Git-based and single-prompt LLM baselines using intent reconstruction, scope detection, and evidence-support metrics. The experimental results demonstrate the effectiveness of combining multiple repository evidence sources with agentic reasoning.\n+\n+## 2. Existing Git tools mainly show what changed, but not the complete context and reasoning behind the code.\n+\n+## 4. Related Work\n+**1. Intent Reconstruction & Commit Untangling**\n+The challenge of deducing developer intent and untangling composite commits has an established lineage in software engineering literature. Early structural and graph-based approaches laid the foundation for rationale-mining from version control histories (Barnett et al., 2015; Dias et al., 2015). More recently, research has shifted toward semantic intent extraction. For instance, Dhaouadi et al. (2023) explored rationale-mining from commit messages via knowledge graphs, while Fan et al. (2024) focused on detecting hidden dependencies. Most relevant to our work is *Atomizer* (Zhu et al., 2026), an LLM-based collaborative multi-agent framework that uses an Intent-Oriented Chain-of-Thought (IO-CoT) strategy to iteratively untangle composite commits. Similarly, *ColaUntangle* (Hou et al., 2024) employs explicit and implicit dependency agents, alongside a reviewer agent, to synthesize commit semantics through iterative consultation.\n+\n+**2. Multi-Stage Reasoning with LLM Agents**\n+The use of specialized LLM agents for interpreting repository semantics has recently gained traction. *VIC-RAGENT* (Chen et al., 2026) proposes a multi-stage reasoning pipeline utilizing specialized \"Code Analyst\" and \"Target Analyst\" agents to detect Vulnerability-Inducing Commits (VICs). \n+\n+**3. Software Project Abandonment & Viability**\n+Prior research heavily relies on fixed inactivity thresholds to classify project abandonment. However, empirical investigations challenge this naive assumption. Avelino et al. (2019) analyzed 1,932 popular GitHub projects, finding that 16% were abandoned by their original core developers, yet 41% of those successfully survived due to community intervention. This indicates that inactivity alone is a volatile signal.\n+\n+## 5. Research Gap\n+Existing approaches generally fall into these categories:\n+- Git tools → show history and structural changes\n+- Code summarization → explains what the code does\n+- LLM QA tools → answer ad-hoc questions about repositories\n+\n+**Gap:** They do not provide one cohesive, evidence-based workflow that combines Code Intent Reconstruction + Scope Creep Detection + Abandoned Project Recovery utilizing multi-agent AI reasoning.\n+\n+## 6. graphs to explain *why* code exists, not just *what* changed.\n+\n+---\n+\n+## 🌟 Key Features\n+\n+1. **🧠 Intent Reconstruction (Intent Agent)**\n+   * Deduces the developer's original intent behind code changes using an Intent-Oriented Chain-of-Thought strategy.\n+   * Provides explicit evidence citations (referencing exact lines of code and commit SHAs) to prove its conclusions.\n+\n+2. **⚠️ Scope Creep Detection (Scope Agent)**\n+   * Compares the stated goal of a commit against the actual structural code changes.\n+   * Flags unrelated file modifications and architectural deviations **Multi-Project Comparison:** Ranks multiple repositories to recommend which project holds the highest technical viability for completion.\n+\n+4. **🕸️ Visual Relationship Graph**\n+   * Renders a +"""Generate only figures supported by actual non-null results."""
+import argparse
+import sys
+from pathlib import Path
+
+ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]
+sys.path.insert(0, str(ROOT))
+from evaluation.dataset import read_json, write_json
+
+
+def generate(output):
+    output = Path(output)
+    result = read_json(output / "final_results.json")
+    raw = read_json(output / "raw" / result["run_id"] / "predictions.json")
+    folder = output / "figures" / result["run_id"]
+    folder.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
+    status = {}
+    try:
+        import matplotlib
+        matplotlib.use("Agg")
+        import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
+    except ImportError:
+        write_json(folder / "manifest.json", {"status": "matplotlib unavailable; no figures fabricated"})
+        return
+    plt.rcParams.update({"font.size": 10, "figure.dpi": 150, "savefig.dpi": 300})
+
+    def save(name, fig):
+        fig.tight_layout()
+        for extension in ("png", "pdf"):
+            fig.savefig(folder / f"{name}.{extension}")
+        plt.close(fig)
+        status[name] = "generated from run " + result["run_id"]
+
+    fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(7, 4.5))
+    for method, summary in result["methods"].items():
+        rows = [r for r in raw if r["method"] == method and r["status"] == "ok"]
+        if rows:
+            ax.scatter([r["code_regions"] for r in rows], [r["total_seconds"] for r in rows], label=summary["name"], alpha=.7)
+    ax.set(xlabel="Input code regions (intent region or diff hunks)", ylabel="Method execution seconds (shared extraction excluded)", title="Observed analysis time" + (" — unscored smoke run" if result["status"] == "unscored_smoke" else ""))
+    if ax.collections:
+        ax.legend(fontsize=8)
+        save("analysis_time", fig)
+    else:
+        plt.close(fig)
+        status["analysis_time"] = "no successful method timings"
+    eligible = [m for m in result["methods"].values() if m["intent"]["accuracy"] is not None]
+    if eligible:
+        fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(7, 4.5))
+        ax.bar([m["name"] for m in eligible], [m["intent"]["accuracy"] for m in eligible])
+        ax.set(ylim=(0, 1), ylabel="Normalized exact-match accuracy", title="Intent reconstruction")
+        save("intent_accuracy", fig)
+    else:
+        status["intent_accuracy"] = "N/A — no scored intent results"
+    eligible = [m for m in result["methods"].values() if any(m["scope"][k] is not None for k in ("precision", "recall", "f1"))]
+    if eligible:
+        fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(8, 4.5))
+        for index, metric in enumerate(("precision", "recall", "f1")):
+            for i, m in enumerate(eligible):
+                if m["scope"][metric] is not None:
+                    ax.bar(i + (index - 1) * .25, m["scope"][metric], width=.23, label=metric if i == 0 else None)
+        ax.set_xticks(range(len(eligible)), [m["name"] for m in eligible])
+        ax.set(ylim=(0, 1), ylabel="Score", title="Scope detection; undefined metrics omitted")
+        ax.legend()
+        save("scope_metrics", fig)
+    else:
+        status["scope_metrics"] = "N/A — no scored scope results"
+    eligible = [m for m in result["methods"].values() if m["recovery"]["ndcg"] is not None]
+    if eligible:
+        fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(7, 4.5))
+        for m in eligible:
+            gold = m["recovery"]["ground_truth_ranking"]
+            predicted = m["recovery"]["predicted_ranking"]
+            ax.scatter(range(1, len(gold) + 1), [predicted.index(c) + 1 for c in gold], label=m["name"])
+        ax.set(xlabel="Ground-truth rank", ylabel="Predicted rank", title="Recovery rankings")
+        ax.legend()
+        save("recovery_rankings", fig)
+    else:
+        status["recovery_rankings"] = "N/A — no measured recovery ranking"
+    write_json(folder / "manifest.json", status)
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
+    parser.add_argument("--output", type=Path, default=ROOT / "evaluation/results")
+    generate(parser.parse_args().output)

+"""Pure metrics. None means unmeasurable, never a fabricated zero."""
+import math
+
+
+def normalized(text):
+    return " ".join(text.casefold().split())
+
+
+def intent_metrics(pairs):
+    if not pairs:
+        return {"accuracy": None, "cases": 0, "correct": 0, "incorrect": 0, "introducing_commit_accuracy": None}
+    correct = sum(normalized(pred.get("intent", "")) in {normalized(x) for x in case["accepted_intents"]} for case, pred in pairs)
+    commits = sum(pred.get("introducing_commit") == case["introducing_commit"] for case, pred in pairs)
+    return {"accuracy": correct / len(pairs), "cases": len(pairs), "correct": correct,
+            "incorrect": len(pairs) - correct, "introducing_commit_accuracy": commits / len(pairs)}
+
+
+def scope_metrics(pairs):
+    tp = fp = fn = unclear = abstentions = correct = decisions = 0
+    for case, pred in pairs:
+        for hunk, gold in case["gold_hunks"].items():
+            value = pred["hunks"].get(hunk, "unclear")
+            abstentions += value == "unclear"
+            if gold == "unclear":
+                unclear += 1
+                continue
+            tp += gold == value == "out-of-scope"
+            fp += gold == "in-scope" and value == "out-of-scope"
+            fn += gold == "out-of-scope" and value != "out-of-scope"
+        if case.get("gold_verdict"):
+            decisions += 1
+            correct += case["gold_verdict"] == pred.get("verdict")
+    precision = tp / (tp + fp) if tp + fp else None
+    recall = tp / (tp + fn) if tp + fn else None
+    f1 = 2 * tp / (2 * tp + fp + fn) if 2 * tp + fp + fn else None
+    return {"tp": tp, "fp": fp, "fn": fn, "precision": precision, "recall": recall, "f1": f1,
+            "gold_unclear_excluded": unclear, "predicted_unclear": abstentions,
+            "decision_accuracy": correct / decisions if decisions else None, "cases": len(pairs)}
+
+
+def recovery_metrics(pairs):
+    if len(pairs) < 2 or any(p.get("score") is None for _, p in pairs):
+        return {"ndcg": None, "repositories": len(pairs), "predicted_ranking": [],
+                "ground_truth_ranking": [c["case_id"] for c, _ in sorted(pairs, key=lambda x: (x[0]["gold_rank"], x[0]["case_id"]))]}
+    ordered = sorted(pairs, key=lambda x: (-x[1]["score"], x[0]["case_id"]))
+    ideal = sorted(pairs, key=lambda x: (-x[0]["gold_recoverability"], x[0]["case_id"]))
+    def dcg(items):
+        return sum((2 ** c["gold_recoverability"] - 1) / math.log2(i + 2) for i, (c, _) in enumerate(items))
+    denominator = dcg(ideal)
+    return {"ndcg": dcg(ordered) / denominator if denominator else None, "repositories": len(pairs),
+            "predicted_ranking": [c["case_id"] for c, _ in ordered],
+            "ground_truth_ranking": [c["case_id"] for c, _ in sorted(pairs, key=lambda x: (x[0]["gold_rank"], x[0]["case_id"]))]}
+
+
+def evidence_metrics(audits):
+    supported = sum(a["supported"] for a in audits)
+    total = sum(a["total_verifiable"] for a in audits)
+    return {"supported": supported, "total_verifiable": total, "rate": supported / total if total else None}

+    if not isinstance(result, dict):
+        raise ValueError("Prediction must be a JSON object")
+    if not isinstance(result.get("claims"), list) or not all(isinstance(c, dict) and isinstance(c.get("text"), str) for c in result["claims"]):
+        raise ValueError("Prediction must include a list of textual claims")
+    for claim in result["claims"]:
+        if any(claim.get(k) is not None and not isinstance(claim[k], str) for k in ("commit", "file", "hunk", "quote", "kind")):
+            raise ValueError("Claim references must be strings or null")
+    if task == "intent":
+        if not isinstance(result.get("intent"), str) or not result["intent"].strip():
+            raise ValueError("Intent prediction must be nonempty text")
+    elif task == "scope":
+        if not isinstance(result.get("hunks"), dict) or set(result["hunks"]) != {h["id"] for h in pack["hunks"]}:
+            raise ValueError("Scope prediction must classify every exact hunk ID")
+        if any(v not in {"in-scope", "out-of-scope", "unclear"} for v in result["hunks"].values()):
+            raise ValueError("Invalid scope class")
+        if result.get("verdict") not in {"keep", "split", "justify"}:
+            raise ValueError("Invalid scope verdict")
+    else:
+        score = result.get("score")
+        if score is not None and (type(score) not in {int, float} or not math.isfinite(score) or not 0 <= score <= 1):
+            raise ValueError("Recovery score must be null or a finite number in [0,1]")
+
+
+def execute(dataset, output, *, smoke=False, live=False, tasks=TASKS):
+    output = Path(output)
+    started = now()
+    clock = time.perf_counter()
+    # No predictions, output replacement, or external calls before dataset validation.
+    data = load_dataset(dataset, allow_unlabelled=smoke, tasks=tasks)
+    preparation_seconds = time.perf_counter() - clock
+    if live and (not os.getenv("GEMINI_API_KEY") or not os.getenv("GEMINI_MODEL")):
+        raise ValueError("Live execution requires GEMINI_API_KEY and an explicit GEMINI_MODEL; no fallback permitted")
+    run_id = datetime.now(timezone.utc).strftime("%Y%m%dT%H%M%S") + "_" + uuid.uuid4().hex[:8]
+    run_path = output / "raw" / run_id
+    raw = []
+    adjudication_templates = []
+    for task in tasks:
+        for case in data["cases"][task]:
+            pack = data["packs"][case["case_id"]]
+            pack_digest = digest(pack)
+            write_json(run_path / "evidence" / f"{case['case_id']}.json", pack)
+            for method in METHODS:

+                    "repository": case["repository"], "commit": case["revision"],
+                    "file": case.get("file"), "region": case.get("region"),
+                    "hunks": [h["id"] for h in pack["hunks"]], "evidence_sha256": pack_digest,
+                    "repositories": 1, "files": pack["file_count"], "commits": pack["commit_count"],
+                    "code_regions": 1 if task == "intent" else len(pack["hunks"]),
+                    "start_time": None, "end_time": None, "total_seconds": None,
+                    "mode": "live" if live and method in {"llm", "aicar"} else "offline"}
+                if method == "llm" and not live:
+                    entry.update(status="skipped", reason="Live LLM execution not enabled")
+                    raw.append(entry)
+                    continue
+                entry["start_time"] = now()
+                tick = time.perf_counter()
+                try:
+                    inputs = copy.deepcopy(pack)
+                    if method == "aicar":
+                        prediction = agentic_system.predict(task, inputs, live=live)
+                    else:
+                        prediction = {"git": git_baseline, "git_script": git_script_baseline, "llm": llm_baseline}[method].predict(task, inputs)
+                    entry["prediction"] = prediction
+                    validate_prediction(task, prediction, pack)
+                    entry.update(status="ok", prediction=prediction, prediction_sha256=prediction_hash(prediction))
+                except Exception as error:
+                    # Do not persist provider exception strings, which can contain credentials/URLs.
+                    entry.update(status="error", reason=type(error).__name__ + ": method failed; no prediction scored")
+                entry["total_seconds"] = time.perf_counter() - tick
+                entry["end_time"] = now()
+                if entry["status"] == "ok":
+                    entry["evidence_audit"] = audit(entry["prediction"], pack)
+                    adjudication_templates.append({"case_id": case["case_id"], "method": method,
+                        "prediction_sha256": entry["prediction_sha256"], "intent_correct": None,
+                        "annotator": None, "rationale": None,
+                        "claims": [{"text": c["claim"]["text"], "supported": None, "rationale": None}
+                                   for c in entry["evidence_audit"]["claims"]]})
+                raw.append(entry)
+    summaries = summarize(data, raw, smoke, tasks)
+    packages = {}
+    for package in ("GitPython", "google-genai", "pytest", "matplotlib"):
+        try:
+            packages[package] = importlib.metadata.version(package)
+        except importlib.metadata.PackageNotFoundError:
+            packages[package] = None
+    root = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]
+    code_files = sorted([*root.glob("evaluation/*.py"), *root.glob("evaluation/runners/*.py"), *root.glob("backend/**/*.py")])
+    provenance = {"python": platform.python_version(), "platform": platform.platform(), "packages": packages,
+        "git_version": git(root, "--version").strip(), "code_revision": git(root, "rev-parse", "HEAD").strip(),
+        "code_sha256": {str(p.relative_to(root)): hashlib.sha256(p.read_bytes()).hexdigest() for p in code_files},
+        "dataset_sha256": {p.name: hashlib.sha256(p.read_bytes()).hexdigest() for p in sorted(Path(dataset).glob("*.json"))},
+        "model": os.getenv("GEMINI_MODEL") if live else None, "temperature": 0 if live else None,
+        "evidence_as_of": data["manifest"]["as_of"]}
+    result = {"schema_version": 1, "run_id": run_id, "status": "unscored_smoke" if smoke else "scored",
+        "start_time": started, "end_time": now(), "total_seconds": time.perf_counter() - clock,
+        "preparation_seconds": preparation_seconds, "timing_scope": "validation/extraction plus method execution; shared extraction is measured separately, report/plot generation excluded",
+        "dataset": data["counts"], "targets_not_observed": TARGETS,
+        "attempts": len(raw), "executed": sum(r["status"] != "skipped" for r in raw),
+        "successful": sum(r["status"] == "ok" for r in raw), "errors": sum(r["status"] == "error" for r in raw),
+        "skipped": sum(r["status"] == "skipped" for r in raw), "scored_cases": 0 if smoke else sum(len(data["cases"][t]) for t in tasks),
+        "methods": summaries, "provenance": provenance}
+    write_json(run_path / "predictions.json", raw)
+    write_json(run_path / "manifest.json", result)
+    write_json(run_path / "review_template.json", adjudication_templates)
+    write_json(output / "processed" / f"{run_id}.json", summaries)
+    return result, raw
+
+
+def summarize(data, raw, smoke, tasks):
+    summaries = {}
+    for method, name in METHODS.items():
+        rows = [r for r in raw if r["method"] == method]
+        pairs = {t: [] for t in TASKS}
+        task_status = {}
+        for task in tasks:
+            selected = [r for r in rows if r["task"] == task]
+            complete = bool(selected) and all(r["status"] == "ok" for r in selected)
+            task_status[task] = "unscored smoke" if smoke else ("complete" if complete else "unavailable: method skipped or failed")
+            if not smoke and complete:
+                mapping = {c["case_id"]: c for c in data["cases"][task]}
+                pairs[task] = [(mapping[r["case_id"]], r["prediction"]) for r in selected]
+                for row in selected:
+                    pair = [(mapping[row["case_id"]], row["prediction"])]
+                    row["metrics"] = intent_metrics(pair) if task == "intent" else scope_metrics(pair) if task == "scope" else None
+        audits = [r["evidence_audit"] for r in rows if r["task"] == "intent" and r["status"] == "ok"] if pairs["intent"] else []
+        summaries[method] = {"name": name, "task_status": task_status,
+            "intent": intent_metrics(pairs["intent"]), "scope": scope_metrics(pairs["scope"]),
+            "recovery": recovery_metrics(pairs["recovery"]), "evidence": evidence_metrics(audits),
+            "analysis_seconds": (sum(r["total_seconds"] for r in rows if r["total_seconds"] is not None)
+                                 if any(r["total_seconds"] is not None for r in rows) else None),
+            "executed": sum(r["status"] != "skipped" for r in rows),
+            "mode": next((r["mode"] for r in rows), None)}
+    return summaries

+"""Add a real local checkout to the dataset; never create semantic labels."""
+import argparse
+import os
+import sys
+from datetime import datetime, timezone
+from pathlib import Path
+
+ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]
+sys.path.insert(0, str(ROOT))
+from backend.services.git_evidence import git, snapshot
+from evaluation.dataset import TASKS, read_json, write_json
+
+
+def prepare(repository, directory, repo_id, limit=4):
+    directory = Path(directory).resolve()
+    repository = Path(repository).resolve()
+    revision = git(repository, "rev-parse", "HEAD").strip()
+    manifest_path = directory / "repositories.json"
+    manifest = read_json(manifest_path) if manifest_path.exists() else {
+        "schema_version": 1, "as_of": datetime.now(timezone.utc).isoformat(), "repositories": []}
+    if any(r["id"] == repo_id or (directory / r["path"]).resolve() == repository for r in manifest["repositories"]):
+        raise ValueError("Repository already registered; existing annotations are never overwritten")
+    try:
+        source = git(repository, "remote", "get-url", "origin").strip()
+    except ValueError:
+        source = str(repository)
+    manifest["repositories"].append({"id": repo_id, "source": source,
+        "path": Path(os.path.relpath(repository, directory)).as_posix(), "revision": revision})
+    cases = {t: read_json(directory / f"{t}_cases.json") if (directory / f"{t}_cases.json").exists() else [] for t in TASKS}
+    pending = {"status": "pending", "annotator": None, "rationale": None}
+    # Include only commits changing source code. Documentation commits are not invented code cases.
+    selected = 0
+    for sha in git(repository, "rev-list", revision).splitlines():
+        changed = git(repository, "diff-tree", "--root", "--no-commit-id", "--name-only", "-r", "--first-parent", sha).splitlines()
+        files = set(git(repository, "ls-tree", "-r", "--name-only", sha).splitlines())
+        source_files = [f for f in changed if f in files and Path(f).name != "__init__.py" and Path(f).suffix in {".py", ".ts", ".tsx", ".js", ".jsx", ".java", ".go", ".rs", ".c", ".cpp"}]
+        if not source_files:
+            continue
+        selected += 1
+        file = sorted(source_files)[0]
+        lines = len(git(repository, "show", f"{sha}:{file}").splitlines())
+        if not lines:
+            continue
+        common = {"repository": repo_id, "revision": sha, "annotation": pending.copy()}
+        cid = f"{repo_id}_intent_{sha[:12]}"
+        case = {**common, "case_id": cid, "file": file, "region": [1, min(lines, 30)],
+                "gold_intent": None, "accepted_intents": [], "introducing_commit": None, "supporting_commits": []}
+        cases["intent"].append(case)
+        pack = snapshot(repository, sha, file=file, region=case["region"], as_of=manifest["as_of"])
+        write_json(directory / "evidence" / f"{cid}.json", pack)
+        cid = f"{repo_id}_scope_{sha[:12]}"
+        if pack["hunks"]:
+            cases["scope"].append({**common, "case_id": cid, "task": None,
+                "task_source": {"reference": None, "text": None}, "diff": pack["diff"],
+                "gold_hunks": {h["id"]: None for h in pack["hunks"]}, "gold_verdict": None})
+            write_json(directory / "evidence" / f"{cid}.json", pack)
+        if selected >= limit:
+            break
+    cid = f"{repo_id}_recovery"
+    cases["recovery"].append({"case_id": cid, "repository": repo_id, "revision": revision,
+        "unfinished": None, "gold_rank": None, "gold_recoverability": None, "annotation": pending.copy()})
+    write_json(directory / "evidence" / f"{cid}.json", snapshot(repository, revision, as_of=manifest["as_of"]))
+    for task in TASKS:
+        write_json(directory / f"{task}_cases.json", cases[task])
+    write_json(manifest_path, manifest)
+    return {t: len(cases[t]) for t in TASKS}
+
+
+def main():
+    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
+    parser.add_argument("--repository", type=Path, default=ROOT)
+    parser.add_argument("--dataset", type=Path, default=ROOT / "evaluation/datasets")
+    parser.add_argument("--id", default="aicar")
+    parser.add_argument("--limit", type=int, default=4)
+    args = parser.parse_args()
+    if args.limit < 1:
+        parser.error("--limit must be positive")
+    try:
+        print(prepare(args.repository, args.dataset, args.id, args.limit))
+    except (ValueError, OSError) as error:
+        parser.exit(2, str(error) + "\n")
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    main()

+# Inspection before implementation
+
+Inspected the original repository at `07b121617c2a064e5e16c43db73a4ee852de864c`.
+The only pre-existing working-tree change was `frontend/package-lock.json`.
+
+1. **Architecture:** React/TypeScript/Vite dashboard, history and comparison pages;
+   Axios through the Vite API proxy; FastAPI endpoints in `backend/main.py`;
+   LangGraph workflow in `backend/graph/workflow.py`; SQLite/SQLAlchemy storage in
+   `backend/database.py` and `backend/models/analysis.py`.
+2. **Existing functionality:** repository cloning and Git extraction, recent
+   commit/file histories, TODO scanning, intent/scope/recovery analysis, narrative
+   report/recommendation agents, health heuristics, persisted analysis history,
+   repository comparison and commit/file graph visualization.
+3. **Actually implemented:** GitPython extraction capped at ten recent commits,
+   five file diffs and truncated patches; evidence-map construction but no evidence
+   verification; scope by filenames rather than hunks; recovery and comparison
+   heuristics, not a validated ranking model. Repository-list endpoint returns
+   mock entries. README's OpenAI description does not match the Gemini code.
+4. **Missing research infrastructure:** pinned real dataset, human labels,
+   provenance, valid evidence support checks, hunk classification, recovery nDCG,
+   baseline parity, raw timing, reproducibility, uncertainty/missing-data handling.
+   Legacy examples contain placeholder SHAs; existing saved results have no
+   corresponding traceable experiment outputs and must not be treated as measured.
+5. **Tests:** manual Markdown checklists and saved PASS examples, no executable
+   automated tests. Frontend provides build/lint scripts. README refers to a
+   missing backend requirements file and incorrect evaluation entry point.
+6. **LLM/fallback:** Gemini SDK, model hardcoded in each agent, clients initialized
+   at import time. `USE_GEMINI_ANALYSIS` defaults false, intent copies the commit
+   message, scope reports insufficient evidence, recovery emits generic medium
+   potential. `.env.example` originally names only `OPENAI_API_KEY`.
+7. **Implementation files:** extend `backend/services/repository_analyzer.py`;
+   add `git_evidence.py`, `llm.py`, `evidence_verifier.py`; extend existing agents
+   with lazy provider access and structured task evaluation; replace legacy
+   backend evaluation entry points/metrics/baselines with a common audited runner;
+   add `evaluation/dataset.py`, `prepare_dataset.py`, `pipeline.py`, `metrics.py`,
+   `reporting.py`, `figures.py`, task runners, datasets, annotation guide and tests.
+
+The paper and FYP draft are intentionally unchanged. Existing dashboard endpoint
+shapes and frontend implementation are preserved.

+# AICAR reproducible evaluation
+
+## Experimental setup
+
+Run `20260922T171748_8f614331`: **unscored_smoke**. Pinned Git objects; shared evidence per case. Python 3.13.9. Model: disabled. All measurements below come from this run.
+
+## Dataset size
+
+{
+  "intent": 3,
+  "scope": 3,
+  "recovery": 1,
+  "repositories": 1,
+  "commits": 4,
+  "labelled": 0,
+  "pending": 7
+}
+
+## Dataset composition
+
+Source paths, origins and immutable revisions: evaluation/datasets/repositories.json. Code-case candidates are commits changing source; recovery eligibility is unconfirmed until annotated. Targets (25 repositories, 40 intent, 30 scope, 20 recovery, approximately 1,800 commits) are not achieved dataset counts.
+
+## Ground-truth methodology
+
+Human annotation is mandatory; see evaluation/ANNOTATION_GUIDE.md. No labels are copied from the paper, legacy examples, commit messages, or model predictions. Intent uses preregistered normalized exact accepted answers; this is a strict textual metric, not a semantic correctness claim. Human semantic review is exported separately and not automatically scored.
+
+## Baselines
+
+Git: commit message extraction; scope abstention; no recovery rank. Git log/blame script: single-origin line-blame message plus history summary; ambiguous provenance abstains. Single-prompt Gemini: one common evidence pack per task, no specialized agent or verifier. Offline runs skip Gemini. No manual human analysis time is claimed.
+
+## AICAR architecture
+
+Existing repository analyzer's pinned-snapshot path, existing intent/scope/recovery agents with structured evaluation outputs, and evidence verifier. Dashboard's LangGraph/report route is not timed. Offline AICAR retains intent message fallback and abstains on semantic scope/recovery. Live outputs use specialized task instructions. This is a task-agent evaluation, not a measured end-to-end dashboard benchmark.
+

software projects.\n+\n+Built with **LangGraph, FastAPI, and React**, this project moves beyond traditional Git tools by synthesizing commit history, structural code patches, and file dependency graphs to explain *why* code exists, not just *what* changed.\n+\n+---\n+\n+## 🌟 Key Features\n+\n+1. **🧠 Intent Reconstruction (Intent Agent)**\n+   * Deduces the developer's original intent behind code changes using an Intent-Oriented Chain-of-Thought strategy.\n+   * Provides explicit evidence citations (referencing exact lines of code and commit SHAs) to prove its conclusions.\n+\n+2. **⚠️ Scope Creep Detection (Scope Agent)**\n+   * Compares the stated goal of a commit against the actual structural code changes.\n+   * Flags unrelated file modifications and architectural deviations that fall outside the bounds of the original task.\n+\n+3. **♻️ Abandoned Project Recovery (Recovery Agent)**\n+   * Analyzes incomplete or abandoned repositories to calculate a heuristic **Health Score**.\n+   * Replaces naive inactivity metrics (like commit frequency or stars) with deep structural indicators like code completeness, unresolved TODOs, and architectural continuity.\n+   * physics-based, 2D force-directed graph connecting commits to their modified files, allowing developers to visually spot high-risk architectural bottlenecks.\n+\n+5. **📊 Empirical Evaluation Suite +      "text": "@@ -0,0 +1,100 @@\n+# 🏺 Agentic Code Archaeology\n+\n+**Agentic Code Archaeology** is an AI-powered, multi-agent system designed to reconstruct the intent behind legacy code, detect scope creep in commits, and evaluate the technical viability of recovering abandoned software projects.\n+\n+Built with **LangGraph, FastAPI, and React**, this project moves beyond traditional Git tools by synthesizing commit history, structural code patches, and file dependency graphs to explain *why* code exists, not just *what* changed.\n+\n+---\n+\n+## 🌟 Key Features\n+\n+1. **🧠 Intent Reconstruction (Intent Agent)**\n+   * Deduces the developer's original intent behind code changes using an Intent-Oriented Chain-of-Thought strategy.\n+   * Provides explicit evidence citations (referencing exact lines of code and commit SHAs) to prove its conclusions.\n+\n+2. **⚠️ Scope Creep Detection (Scope Agent)**\n+   * Compares the stated goal of a commit against the actual structural code changes.\n+   * Flags unrelated file modifications and architectural deviations that fall outside the bounds of the original task.\n+\n+3. **♻️ Abandoned Project Recovery (Recovery Agent)**\n+   * Analyzes incomplete or abandoned repositories to calculate a heuristic **Health Score**.\n+   * Replaces naive inactivity metrics (like commit frequency or stars) with deep structural indicators like code completeness, unresolved TODOs, and architectural continuity.\n+   * **Multi-Project Comparison:** Ranks multiple repositories to recommend which project holds the highest technical viability for completion.\n+\n+4. **🕸️ Visual Relationship Graph**\n+   * Renders a physics-based, 2D force-directed graph connecting commits to their modified files, allowing developers to visually spot high-risk architectural bottlenecks.\n+\n+5. **📊 Empirical Evaluation Suite (Research Ready)**\n+   * Includes a built-in evaluation framework for academic research.\n+   * Compares the Agentic System's accuracy against standard Git Baselines and zero-shot LLM Baselines.\n+\n+---\n+\n+## 🏗️ System Architecture\n+\n+* **Backend:** FastAPI, Python, SQLite\n+* **AI Orchestration:** LangGraph (State-machine driven multi-agent workflow), OpenAI API\n+* **Frontend:** React, Vite, CSS Grid, `react-force-graph-2d`\n+\n+---\n+\n+## 🚀 Getting Started\n+\n+### Prerequisites\n+* Python 3.10+\n+* An Agentic AI Framework for Code Intent Analysis, Scope Creep Detection, and Software Project Recovery\n+\n+## 1. Abstract\n+Understanding the historical intent behind software code is challenging because conventional version-control tools primarily describe what changed rather than why a change was introduced. Developers may also struggle to identify changes that exceed the original task scope and to assess whether abandoned software projects are worth recovering. This work proposes an agentic AI framework that analyzes Git repository history, code diffs, file evolution, and repository metadata to reconstruct code intent, detect potential scope creep, and assess project recovery potential. The framework uses specialized AI agents coordinated through a LangGraph workflow-based architecture and produces evidence-linked conclusions. The system is evaluated against Git-based and single-prompt LLM baselines using intent reconstruction, scope detection, and evidence-support metrics. The experimental results demonstrate the effectiveness of combining multiple repository evidence sources with agentic reasoning.\n+\n+## 2. Problem Statement\n+Developers often struggle to understand why old code was written, identify changes that go beyond the original task, and decide which abandoned software project is worth completing. Existing Git tools mainly show what changed, but not the complete context and reasoning behind the code.\n+\n+## 4. Related Work\n+**1. Intent Reconstruction & Commit Untangling**\n+The challenge of deducing developer intent and untangling composite commits has an established lineage in software engineering literature. Early structural and graph-based approaches laid the foundation for rationale-mining from version control histories (Barnett et al., 2015; Dias et al., 2015). More recently, research has shifted toward semantic intent extraction. For instance, Dhaouadi et al. (2023) explored rationale-mining from commit messages via knowledge graphs, while Fan et al. (2024) focused on detecting hidden dependencies. Most relevant to our work is *Atomizer* (Zhu et al., 2026), an LLM-based collaborative multi-agent framework that uses an Intent-Oriented Chain-of-Thought (IO-CoT) strategy to iteratively untangle composite commits. Similarly, *ColaUntangle* (Hou et al., 2024) employs explicit and implicit dependency agents, alongside a reviewer agent, to synthesize commit semantics through iterative consultation.\n+\n+**2. Multi-Stage Reasoning with LLM Agents**\n+The use of specialized LLM agents for interpreting repository semantics has recently gained traction. *VIC-RAGENT* (Chen et al., 2026) proposes a multi-stage reasoning pipeline utilizing specialized \"Code Analyst\" and \"Target Analyst\" agents to detect Vulnerability-Inducing Commits (VICs). \n+\n+**3. Software Project Abandonment & Viability**\n+Prior research heavily relies on fixed inactivity thresholds to classify project abandonment. However, empirical investigations challenge this naive assumption. Avelino et al. (2019) analyzed 1,932 popular GitHub projects, finding that 16% were abandoned by their original core developers, yet 41% of those successfully survived due to community intervention. This indicates that inactivity alone is a volatile signal.\n+\n+## 5. Research Gap\n+Existing approaches generally fall into these categories:\n+- Git tools → show history and structural changes\n+- Code summarization → explains what the code does\n+- LLM QA tools → answer ad-hoc questions about repositories\n+\n+**Gap:** They do not provide one cohesive, evidence-based workflow that combines Code Intent Reconstruction + Scope Creep Detection + Abandoned Project Recovery utilizing multi-agent AI reasoning.\n+\n+## 6. An Agentic AI Framework for Code Intent Analysis, Scope Creep Detection, and Software Project Recovery\n+\n+## 1. Abstract\n+Understanding the historical intent behind software code is challenging because conventional version-control tools primarily describe what changed rather than why a change was introduced. Developers may also struggle to identify changes that exceed the original task scope and to assess whether abandoned software projects are worth recovering. This work proposes an agentic AI framework that analyzes Git repository history, code diffs, file evolution, and repository metadata to reconstruct code intent, detect potential scope creep, and assess project recovery potential. The framework uses specialized AI agents coordinated through a LangGraph workflow-based architecture and produces evidence-linked conclusions. The system is evaluated against Git-based and single-prompt LLM baselines using intent reconstruction, scope detection, and evidence-support metrics. The experimental results demonstrate the effectiveness of combining multiple repository evidence sources with agentic reasoning.\n+\n+## 2. Introduction\n+[To be expanded based on problem statement...]\n+\n+## 3. Problem Statement\n+Developers often struggle to understand why old code was written, identify changes that go beyond the original task, and decide which abandoned software project is worth completing. Existing Git tools mainly show what changed, but not the complete context and reasoning behind the code.\n+\n+## 4. Related Work\n+**1. Intent Reconstruction & Commit Untangling**\n+The challenge of deducing developer intent and untangling composite commits has an established lineage in software engineering literature. Early structural and graph-based approaches laid the foundation for rationale-mining from version control histories (Barnett et al., 2015; Dias et al., 2015). More recently, research has shifted toward semantic intent extraction. For instance, Dhaouadi et al. (2023) explored rationale-mining from commit messages via knowledge graphs, while Fan et al. (2024) focused on detecting hidden dependencies. Most relevant to our work is *Atomizer* (Zhu et al., 2026), an LLM-based collaborative multi-agent framework that uses an Intent-Oriented Chain-of-Thought (IO-CoT) strategy to iteratively untangle composite commits. Similarly, *ColaUntangle* (Hou et al., 2024) employs explicit and implicit dependency agents, alongside a reviewer agent, to synthesize commit semantics through iterative consultation.\n+\n+**2. Multi-Stage Reasoning with LLM Agents**\n+The use of specialized LLM agents for interpreting repository semantics has recently gained traction. *VIC-RAGENT* (Chen et al., 2026) proposes a multi-stage reasoning pipeline utilizing specialized \"Code Analyst\" and \"Target Analyst\" agents to detect Vulnerability-Inducing Commits (VICs). \n+\n+**3. Software Project Abandonment & Viability**\n+Prior research heavily relies on fixed inactivity thresholds to classify project abandonment. However, empirical investigations challenge this naive assumption. Avelino et al. (2019) analyzed 1,932 popular GitHub projects, finding that 16% were abandoned by their original core developers, yet 41% of those successfully survived due to community intervention. This indicates that inactivity alone is a volatile signal.\n+\n+## 5. Research Gap\n+Existing approaches generally fall into these categories:\n+- Git tools → show history and structural changes\n+- Code summarization → explains what the code does\n+- LLM QA tools → answer ad-hoc questions about repositories\n+\n+**Gap:** They do not provide one cohesive, evidence-based workflow that combines Code Intent Reconstruction + Scope Creep Detection + Abandoned Project Recovery utilizing multi-agent AI reasoning.\n+\n+## 6. Proposed Methodology & System Architecture\n+\n+```text\n+                 Git Repository\n+                       │\n+                       ▼\n+              Repository Analyzer\n+                       │\n+        ┌──────────────┼──────────────┐\n+        ▼              ▼              ▼\n+   Commit History   Code Diffs    File History\n+        │              │              │\n+        └──────────────┼──────────────┘\n+                       ▼\n+                Agent Workflow (LangGraph)\n+                       │\n+        ┌──────────────┼──────────────┐\n+        ▼              ▼              ▼\n+   Intent Agent    Scope Agent   Recovery Agent\n+        │              │              │\n+        └──────────────┼──────────────┘\n+                       ▼\n+             Evidence-Based Results\n+                       │\n+                       ▼\n+          Dashboard + Recommendations\n+```\n+\n+## 7. software projects.\n+\n+Built with **LangGraph, FastAPI, and React**, this project moves beyond traditional Git tools by synthesizing commit history, structural code patches, and file dependency graphs to explain *why* code exists, not just *what* changed.\n+\n+---\n+\n+## 🌟 Key Features\n+\n+1. **🧠 Intent Reconstruction (Intent Agent)**\n+   * Deduces the developer's original intent behind +      "text": "@@ -0,0 +1,100 @@\n+# 🏺 Agentic Code Archaeology\n+\n+**Agentic Code Archaeology** is an AI-powered, multi-agent system designed to reconstruct the intent behind legacy code, detect scope creep in commits, and evaluate the technical viability of recovering abandoned software projects.\n+\n+Built with **LangGraph, FastAPI, and React**, this project moves beyond traditional Git tools by synthesizing commit history, structural code patches, and file dependency graphs to explain *why* code exists, not just *what* changed.\n+\n+---\n+\n+## 🌟 Key Features\n+\n+1. **🧠 Intent Reconstruction (Intent Agent)**\n+   * Deduces the developer's original intent behind code changes using an Intent-Oriented Chain-of-Thought strategy.\n+   * Provides explicit evidence citations (referencing exact lines of code and commit SHAs) to prove its conclusions.\n+\n+2. **⚠️ Scope Creep Detection (Scope Agent)**\n+   * Compares the stated goal of a commit against the actual structural code changes.\n+   * Flags unrelated file modifications and architectural deviations that fall outside the bounds of the original task.\n+\n+3. **♻️ Abandoned Project Recovery (Recovery Agent)**\n+   * Analyzes incomplete or abandoned repositories to calculate a heuristic **Health Score**.\n+   * Replaces naive inactivity metrics (like commit frequency or stars) with deep structural indicators like code completeness, unresolved TODOs, and architectural continuity.\n+   * **Multi-Project Comparison:** Ranks multiple repositories to recommend which project holds the highest technical viability for completion.\n+\n+4. **🕸️ Visual Relationship Graph**\n+   * Renders a physics-based, 2D force-directed graph connecting commits to their modified files, allowing developers to visually spot high-risk architectural bottlenecks.\n+\n+5. **📊 Empirical Evaluation Suite (Research Ready)**\n+   * Includes a built-in evaluation framework for academic research.\n+   * Compares the Agentic System's accuracy against standard Git Baselines and zero-shot LLM Baselines.\n+\n+---\n+\n+## 🏗️ System Architecture\n+\n+* **Backend:** FastAPI, Python, SQLite\n+* **AI Orchestration:** LangGraph An Agentic AI Framework for Code Intent Analysis, Scope Creep Detection, and Software Project Recovery\n+\n+## 1. Abstract\n+Understanding the historical intent behind software code is challenging because conventional version-control tools primarily describe what changed rather than why a change was introduced. Developers may also struggle to identify changes that exceed the original task scope and to assess whether abandoned software projects are worth recovering. This work proposes an agentic AI framework that analyzes Git repository history, code diffs, file evolution, and repository metadata to reconstruct code intent, detect potential scope creep, and assess project recovery potential. The framework uses specialized AI agents coordinated through a LangGraph workflow-based architecture and produces evidence-linked conclusions. The system is evaluated against Git-based and single-prompt LLM baselines using intent reconstruction, scope detection, and evidence-support metrics. The experimental results demonstrate the effectiveness of combining multiple repository evidence sources with agentic reasoning.\n+\n+## 2. Problem Statement\n+Developers often struggle to understand why old code was written, identify changes that go beyond the original task, and decide which abandoned software project is worth completing. Existing Git tools mainly show what changed, but not the complete context and reasoning behind the code.\n+\n+## 4. Related Work\n+**1. Intent Reconstruction & Commit Untangling**\n+The challenge of deducing developer intent and untangling composite commits has an established lineage in software engineering literature. Early structural and graph-based approaches laid the foundation for rationale-mining from version control histories (Barnett et al., 2015; Dias et al., 2015). More recently, research has shifted toward semantic intent extraction. For instance, Dhaouadi et al. (2023) explored rationale-mining from commit messages via knowledge graphs, while Fan et al. (2024) focused on detecting hidden dependencies. Most relevant to our work is *Atomizer* (Zhu et al., 2026), an LLM-based collaborative multi-agent framework that uses an Intent-Oriented Chain-of-Thought (IO-CoT) strategy to iteratively untangle composite commits. Similarly, *ColaUntangle* (Hou et al., 2024) employs explicit and implicit dependency agents, alongside a reviewer agent, to synthesize commit semantics through iterative consultation.\n+\n+**2. Multi-Stage Reasoning with LLM Agents**\n+The use of specialized LLM agents for interpreting repository semantics has recently gained traction. *VIC-RAGENT* (Chen et al., 2026) proposes a multi-stage reasoning pipeline utilizing specialized \"Code Analyst\" and \"Target Analyst\" agents to detect Vulnerability-Inducing Commits (VICs). \n+\n+**3. Software Project Abandonment & Viability**\n+Prior research heavily relies on fixed inactivity thresholds to classify project abandonment. However, empirical investigations challenge this naive assumption. Avelino et al. (2019) analyzed 1,932 popular GitHub projects, finding that 16% were abandoned by their original core developers, yet 41% of those successfully survived due to community intervention. This indicates that inactivity alone is a volatile signal.\n+\n+## 5. Research Gap\n+Existing approaches generally fall into these categories:\n+- Git tools → show history and structural changes\n+- Code summarization → explains what the code does\n+- LLM QA tools → answer ad-hoc questions about repositories\n+\n+**Gap:** They do not provide one cohesive, evidence-based workflow that combines Code Intent Reconstruction + Scope Creep Detection + Abandoned Project Recovery utilizing multi-agent AI reasoning.\n+\n+## 6. Proposed Methodology & System Architecture\n+\n+```text\n+                 Git Repository\n+                       │\n+                       ▼\n+              Repository Analyzer\n+                       │\n+        ┌──────────────┼──────────────┐\n+        ▼              ▼              ▼\n+   Commit History   Code Diffs    File History\n+        │              │              │\n+        └──────────────┼──────────────┘\n+                       ▼\n+                Agent Workflow (LangGraph)\n+                       │\n+        ┌──────────────┼──────────────┐\n+        ▼              ▼              ▼\n+   Intent Agent    Scope Agent   Recovery Agent\n+        │              │              │\n+        └──────────────┼──────────────┘\n+                       ▼\n+             Evidence-Based Results\n+                       │\n+                       ▼\n+          Dashboard + Recommendations\n+```\n+\n+## 7. An Agentic AI Framework for Code Intent Analysis, Scope Creep Detection, and Software Project Recovery\n+\n+## 1. Abstract\n+Understanding the historical intent behind software code is challenging because conventional version-control tools primarily describe what changed rather than why a change was introduced. Developers may also struggle to identify changes that exceed the original task scope and to assess whether abandoned software projects are worth recovering. This work proposes an agentic AI framework that analyzes Git repository history, code diffs, file evolution, and repository metadata to reconstruct code intent, detect potential scope creep, and assess project recovery potential. The framework uses specialized AI agents coordinated through a LangGraph workflow-based architecture and produces evidence-linked conclusions. The system is evaluated against Git-based and single-prompt LLM baselines using intent reconstruction, scope detection, and evidence-support metrics. The experimental results demonstrate the effectiveness of combining multiple repository evidence sources with agentic reasoning.\n+\n+## 2.
